Job Description
We are looking for a Mapping Engineer to own the creation and validation of the high-definition maps that our autonomous tractors drive on. AeroVect builds category-defining autonomy for airport airside operations, and every deployment depends on accurate, safe, production-grade maps of structured, low-speed environments — taxiways, aircraft stands, and indoor baggage halls.
This is a hands-on, end-to-end ownership role based on-site in Atlanta. You'll be the single point of contact for incoming mapping requests, build and update maps through our map repository and Map CI pipeline, and validate map changes in simulation and on the tractor here in Atlanta before it ships. You'll work closely with autonomy, operations, and test engineers, and report into the mapping/autonomy team.
This is an excellent entry point for someone early in their career who is detail-obsessed, wants to work close to real hardware, and is excited to own a process from request to deployment. We'll train you on our tools — what matters most is rigor, reliability, and a strong sense of ownership.

Submit map changes as pull requests through the map repository, following our "maps as code" workflow and getting them green through Map CI (validation, connectivity, and path-feasibility checks).
Validate every change in simulation first, then test on the tractor in Atlanta as needed.
Capture evidence (sim videos, test results, before/after diffs) and document testing results
Maintain map hygiene — pruning duplicates, keeping naming and versioning consistent, and documenting the process so it scales beyond one person.
Coordinate with external mapping vendors to validate and integrate large-scale map deliveries.

Basic scripting ability (Python preferred) and comfort working on Linux and the command line.
A strong sense of ownership, clear written communication, and the ability to keep a request queue organized under shifting priorities.
Based in or willing to relocate to Atlanta, and comfortable working on-site with the vehicle.
We Prefer:
Experience with mapping or GIS tools (JOSM, QGIS, OpenStreetMap) or HD map formats (Lanelet2, OpenDRIVE).
Exposure to ROS / ROS2 and autonomy stacks
Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, AWS S3, or simulation tools such as CARLA.
Geospatial fundamentals: coordinate frames, aerial imagery alignment, point clouds.
Experience working in a fast-moving startup environment.

Description
Amazon Advertising is a multi-billion-dollar business and one of the fastest-growing at Amazon. The Autonomous Development team within Ads AI Core Infra (ACI) org is reinventing how advertising software gets built: we develop AI agents and developer-intelligence systems that write, review, and ship production code across the Ads org. If you want to work at the frontier of agentic software development — where large language models do the implementation and engineers design the systems that make them correct, safe, and scalable — this is the team.
We are looking for an experienced Software Development Engineer to build the platforms behind autonomous software delivery. Our systems already index tens of thousands of software pipelines to give engineers and AI agents grounded, up-to-date answers about how Amazon's code actually works; they generate code changes directly from feature specifications; and they take real engineering intake from partner teams and deliver working, reviewed code with minimal human involvement. You will design the services, data platforms, and evaluation infrastructure that let these agents operate reliably at Amazon scale.
This is high-ownership, high-impact work. The problems span distributed systems, large-scale data and retrieval, LLM orchestration, and the evaluation frameworks that let us trust autonomous output enough to ship it. You will build systems that thousands of builders depend on every week, and your work will directly move how fast the entire Ads org can turn an idea into shipped software.

Develop agentic code-generation systems that turn specifications into reviewed, production-ready code changes

Drive technical design for ambiguous, greenfield problems and raise the engineering bar through design and code reviews

Mentor other engineers and help raise the team's technical bar
About The Team
We are the Autonomous Development team within the Ads AI Core Infra (ACI) organization at Amazon Advertising. Our mission is simple to state and hard to do: change how advertising software gets built, so that an idea can become shipped, production-quality code faster than ever before. We build the agents and developer-intelligence platforms that the rest of the Ads org relies on to move quickly and correctly.
We operate at the frontier of agentic software development, where large language models do the implementation and engineers design the systems that make that output correct, safe, and scalable. Our work is genuinely greenfield — there is no playbook for grounding LLMs in massive, constantly-changing codebases or for trusting autonomous code enough to ship it. We figure it out, build it, and put it in front of thousands of builders.
Culturally, we value deep ownership, strong engineering judgment, and learning fast over being right the first time. Engineers here own meaningful systems end to end, work directly with applied scientists and partner teams across the org, and have an outsized impact on how Amazon Advertising delivers software. We care about each other, default to candor, and keep the bar high while staying a team people genuinely enjoy being part of. If you're excited to build the systems that make autonomous software delivery real at Amazon scale, you'll fit right in.

Mapbox is the leading real-time location platform for a new generation of location-aware businesses. Mapbox is the only platform that equips organizations with the full set of tools to power the navigation of people, packages, and vehicles everywhere. More than 4 million registered developers have chosen Mapbox because of the platform’s flexibility, security and privacy compliance. Organizations use Mapbox applications, data, SDKs and APIs to create customized and immersive experiences that delight their customers.
What We Do
The Search Box - Offline Search team is responsible for building a robust, high-performance search engine that empowers mobile and automotive customers to find places, addresses, and points of interest seamlessly, even in environments with zero network connectivity. We do this by engineering highly optimized on-device search algorithms, developing advanced data compression and efficient delta update mechanisms, and creating lightweight, scalable tile-based solutions that deliver low-latency results on constrained hardware. Our work ensures that users—from drivers navigating remote highways to mobile users in dense urban dead zones—experience a reliable, fast, and consistent search experience wherever they go.
As AI becomes embedded in modern engineering workflows, we value engineers who can thoughtfully integrate AI into design, development, and decision-making. Our interview process will include discussion of how you use AI in your engineering workflow.
What You'll Do
Joining us as a Software Engineer on the Offline Search team, you will play a critical role in bringing world-class search capabilities to embedded systems and mobile devices operating without network connectivity. You will bring your expertise in systems engineering and performance optimization to a passionate, cross-functional team focused on the automotive and mobile mapping space.
Design, code, and optimize core search algorithms tailored for on-device execution, ensuring high-speed query resolution under strict CPU, memory, and storage constraints.
Take ownership of complex offline data delivery systems, designing and implementing advanced tile compression techniques (e.g., Zstd) and efficient delta update pipelines to minimize payload sizes.
Collaborate across multiple R&D and backend teams to seamlessly integrate data processing pipelines and ensure parity between our cloud and offline search products.
Engage directly with trend-setting automotive OEMs in EU, US, Japan, and China, as well as suppliers like automotive Tier 1 companies and Mapping firms to understand hardware specifications, troubleshoot integration challenges, and align technical deliverables with their rollout schedules.
Collect and monitor deep system telemetry to evaluate performance tradeoffs (e.g., CPU utilization vs. query latency), establish baselines, and drive continuous architectural improvements.
Play a key role in defining the technical roadmap, scoping complex features, and writing technical design documents for next-generation offline search capabilities.
What We Believe Are Important Traits For This Role
You are located in the Eastern Time Zone.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
Strong proficiency in C++ (our core engine language), with a solid understanding of memory management, multi-threading, and systems-level programming.
Experience with Python or other scripting languages commonly used for tooling, data processing, or test automation.
Proven experience analyzing and optimizing code for performance-constrained environments, thoughtfully balancing tradeoffs between CPU utilization, memory consumption, and query latency.
Familiarity with data structures, algorithmic efficiency, and binary data formats (experience with data compression like Zstd or delta update mechanisms is a strong plus).
Strong analytical thinking and the ability to justify technical decisions using system telemetry and data.
Meticulous attention to detail and a creative, resourceful approach to problem-solving.
Excellent communication skills in English, with a proven ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional engineering, product, and data teams.
Nice to Have Traits for This Role
Prior experience in the mapping, navigation, or automotive industry.
Knowledge of machine learning techniques for geospatial data analysis.
Contributions to open-source geospatial or data analysis projects.

We value high-performing creative individuals who dig into problems and opportunities.

We emphasize an environment of teaching and learning to equip employees with the tools needed to be successful in their function and the company.

The Role:
Founding Engineer, GovTech
There is no existing playbook for moving billions of dollars of state-administered education funds through a consumer card product — you will be one of the people who writes it. As Founding Engineer, you will own every dollar that moves through the company's stack, from card issuing to disbursements, reconciliation, and regulatory reporting, and you will make the architecture calls yourself rather than inherit someone else's system. This is a founding seat working directly alongside the co-founders, not a slot on an existing infra team.
As Founding Engineer, you will:
Payment Systems Architecture: Design and own a multi-service monorepo spanning an event-driven pipeline, a payments API (onboarding, credit, cards), balance healthchecks, and regulatory reporting jobs, from the ground up. Make the architecture-level decisions on how to securely and reliably handle billions of dollars in state-funded educational payments, including card issuing infrastructure, processor integrations, and fraud and credit risk controls.
Design a money movement flow: ledgered internal state, transaction lifecycle management, idempotency, retries, and deterministic replay so we can reason about every flow.
Build high-trust, reliable reconciliation: daily/continuous reconciliation between internal ledger, card network events, banking events, and vendor/provider reports — and the tooling to investigate mismatches fast.
Minimize operational risk: build guardrails that prevent bad states (double-spend, duplicate webhook processing, inconsistent balances, orphaned settlements) as the system scales from hundreds to hundreds of thousands of users.
Ledger Integrity Reconciliation: Be responsible for keeping independent ledgers aligned at all times despite asynchronous event processing. You will build the automated healthcheck and reconciliation systems that catch discrepancies the moment they appear, because none exist yet

Obsessive About Correctness: You know that a missing cent compounds into a crisis. Retries don't erase history, idempotency is deliberate, and validation belongs where truth lives — the database.
Assumes the Real World is Unreliable: Banks go down, queues back up, vendors change APIs without warning. You build systems that stay predictable anyway.
Craves Ownership: You want to be the single person everyone trusts when money is moving. You're not looking to contribute to a system — you want to have engineered it.

Experience with Lithic, Column, LoanPro, Stripe Issuing, or comparable card and banking infrastructure is a strong plus

We are looking for an exceptional Senior Software Engineer to architect and build the foundational data infrastructure that will serve as the brain of a project ecosystem.
We are not looking for someone to stitch together off-the-shelf data frameworks. You will be responsible for designing highly novel data models and processing pipelines capable of handling massive quantities of output data from complex simulations.

Architect the Data Ensemble: Design and implement the architecture to ensemble various sources of injected context (deeply structural simulation data, historical game states, and dynamic user inputs) into a unified, highly queryable format optimized for LLM consumption.
Massive Batch Infrastructure: Build highly scalable, resilient data architectures from scratch. You will optimize for moving, transforming, and processing massive quantities of simulation output data via enormous batch jobs, maintaining the minimal latency required for rapid wargame iterations.
Complex Data Modeling: Design sophisticated, highly relational data models that accurately represent massive, state-based simulation environments, making them easily interpretable by machine learning models.
First-Principles Problem Solving: Navigate highly ambiguous product requirements to design custom, ground-up systems where existing open-source or enterprise tools simply cannot handle the structural complexity or scale.
Technical Leadership: Set the technical standard for the data infrastructure team, driving rigorous code quality, system performance, and architectural clarity.

Experience: 5+ years of backend or data infrastructure experience, operating at a Senior, Staff, or Principal level.
Engineering Excellence: Deep, expert-level proficiency in systems languages (e.g., Rust, Go, C++, or highly optimized Python/Java, Spark, PySpark) and a fundamental understanding of memory management, compute limits, and distributed systems architecture.
High-Throughput / Low-Latency Data: Proven track record of processing massive datasets. You understand how to optimize massive batch jobs and parallel processing across distributed simulation nodes without sacrificing speed.

Search & RecSys: Building complex information retrieval systems or recommendation engines.
Gaming / MMOs: Managing complex state, data relationships, and telemetry for massive, highly populated simulations.
High-Frequency Trading (HFT): Processing disparate, massive streams of data for algorithmic decision-making.
Mission-Driven: A strong desire to build robust, foundational technology that supports national security and defense modernization.
Nice to Have

The Role
We are looking for an exceptional Senior Software Engineer to architect and build the foundational data infrastructure that will serve as the brain of a project ecosystem.
We are not looking for someone to stitch together off-the-shelf data frameworks. You will be responsible for designing highly novel data models and processing pipelines capable of handling massive quantities of output data from complex simulations.
At the core of this role is the challenge of building a foundational data ensemble—a unified architecture that seamlessly aggregates, structures, and stages diverse sources of simulation outputs and user inputs. Your systems will manage enormous batch throughput jobs with strict, minimal latency requirements, ensuring that downstream AI systems and language models have the exact context they need to actionably reason over complex, multi-dimensional scenarios.
Key Responsibilities
Architect the Data Ensemble: Design and implement the architecture to ensemble various sources of injected context (deeply structural simulation data, historical game states, and dynamic user inputs) into a unified, highly queryable format optimized for LLM consumption.
Massive Batch Infrastructure: Build highly scalable, resilient data architectures from scratch. You will optimize for moving, transforming, and processing massive quantities of simulation output data via enormous batch jobs, maintaining the minimal latency required for rapid wargame iterations.
Complex Data Modeling: Design sophisticated, highly relational data models that accurately represent massive, state-based simulation environments, making them easily interpretable by machine learning models.
First-Principles Problem Solving: Navigate highly ambiguous product requirements to design custom, ground-up systems where existing open-source or enterprise tools simply cannot handle the structural complexity or scale.
Technical Leadership: Set the technical standard for the data infrastructure team, driving rigorous code quality, system performance, and architectural clarity.
What We’re Looking For
Experience: 5+ years of backend or data infrastructure experience, operating at a Senior, Staff, or Principal level.
Engineering Excellence: Deep, expert-level proficiency in systems languages (e.g., Rust, Go, C++, or highly optimized Python/Java, Spark, PySpark) and a fundamental understanding of memory management, compute limits, and distributed systems architecture.
High-Throughput / Low-Latency Data: Proven track record of processing massive datasets. You understand how to optimize massive batch jobs and parallel processing across distributed simulation nodes without sacrificing speed.
Information Retrieval & Context Surfacing: You don't need a background in AI agents, but you must be an expert in surfacing the right needle from an ocean of hay to feed decision-making engines. We highly value engineers with backgrounds in:
Search & RecSys: Building complex information retrieval systems or recommendation engines.
Gaming / MMOs: Managing complex state, data relationships, and telemetry for massive, highly populated simulations.
High-Frequency Trading (HFT): Processing disparate, massive streams of data for algorithmic decision-making.
Mission-Driven: A strong desire to build robust, foundational technology that supports national security and defense modernization.
Nice to Have
Security Clearance: An active Secret or TS/SCI clearance is a nice to have for this role. If you do not have an active clearance, you must be eligible and willing to obtain one.
Experience with LLM context optimization, vector embeddings, or agentic AI frameworks (e.g., advanced RAG architectures).
Deep domain experience working with wargaming data, complex systems modeling, or distributed simulation protocols.
Previous experience in a high-growth, 0-to-1 startup environment.

Legence (Nasdaq: LGN) is a leading provider of engineering, consulting, installation, and maintenance services for mission-critical systems in buildings. The company specializes in designing, fabricating, and installing complex HVAC, process piping, and other mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems—enhancing energy efficiency, reliability, and sustainability in new and existing facilities. Legence also delivers long-term performance through strategic upgrades and holistic solutions. Serving some of the world’s most technically demanding sectors, Legence counts over 60% of the Nasdaq-100 Index among its clients.
